summary: Lafayette sits in a sun-drenched fold of the East Bay hills where the terrain is emphatically not flat — oak-studded ridgelines rise on three sides, and from higher elevations Mount Diablo looms to the east like a personal landmark, its 3,849-foot summit close enough to hike before lunch. Despite that semi-rural topography, BART's Lafayette station drops riders into downtown San Francisco in roughly 35 minutes, making this a textbook bedroom community where the median household pulls in $222,393 yet almost certainly commutes west for work — local employment options are thin, tilted toward small professional offices and retail rather than any single large employer. The affordability math is striking even by Bay Area standards: median home values exceed $2 million, putting the price-to-income ratio above 9:1, a figure that makes even the area's high incomes look modest against a mortgage. The compact downtown along Mt. Diablo Boulevard offers a genuine walkable stretch of coffee shops, restaurants, and a well-regarded farmers' market, but step two blocks in any direction and you're on winding, sidewalk-free residential roads carved into hillsides. With 9.3 hours of daily sunshine, mild year-round temperatures averaging 68°F daytime highs, and direct trail access into the Lafayette-Moraga Regional Trail and Briones Regional Park, outdoor life is effortless and constant. Lafayette is essentially a place where extraordinary natural setting and transit access are capitalized almost entirely into housing cost — the landscape is the amenity, and the price tag is the admission.
